verdict.rationale: The skills are files you install or copy into your own repo's `.claude/skills/`, and the helper scripts are local standard-library Python that don't touch the network. That means the core artifacts run under the user's control. However, execution depends on Claude Code or a chat LLM, and nothing documents fully self-contained self-hosting. Missing for 10: explicit self-hosting docs, a stated open-source license, running without a hosted LLM, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's `.claude/skills/`.
Six of them, all standard-library Python. None touch the network.
Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the top of a chat and it runs as a mode.
